note: Vol. I No. 20, and the issue that counts the building season: `Seven or eight buildings have been raised in this town within the past week` (c001). Sixteen of thirty-two segmenter columns are the Tesseract fallback and all eight of page 4's are, so the town is read from page 2 column 8 and page 3 columns 1 and 2. What page 3 column 2 holds is the May-term court docket, and it is worth more than the advertising around it: two attachment suits that place a dwelling house by lot and block, a shed in the rear of a Beaubien store house, and twenty-odd lots and blocks of section 16 by number. Beside them, John H. Kinzie's warehouse OPPOSITE FORT DEARBORN and P. B. F. Cable's first notice that he has taken the Eagle Hotel — the same advertisement T-0289 read three months later in July. THE PAGE THIS READING NEVER OPENED HELD THE MONTH'S CENTREPIECE (T-0321, 2026-08-29). Page 4 columns 2 and 3 carry the THIRD printing of the list of letters remaining in the Post Office at Chicago on 1 April 1834, read now as c016 and c017. The sentence above — 'all eight of page 4's are [fallback], so the town is read from page 2 column 8 and page 3 columns 1 and 2' — is the whole explanation: a fallback column is worse, not empty, and the second half of this list is the cleanest witness to the 1 April return the corpus holds, one name per line with no debris at all.

claims.normalized: Seven or eight buildings have [b]een rais[ed in] this town within the past week.
claims.notes: A COUNT, DATED, OF THE FABRIC GOING UP. Two lines, and they are the most useful sentence April 1834 prints for a reconstruction: seven or eight raisings in the week before 16 April 1834, in a town whose plat this project builds. It follows the same paper's notice a week earlier that the mechanics were at work and others were arranging to put buildings up (1834-04-08 c003), and neither says WHERE, so this is a rate and not a placement — nothing may be sited from it. The column is one of the eleven on this issue's page 2 that the Vision reader completed, which is why the sentence survives whole while most of the month's advertising does not; the lines are NOT interleaved.

claims.notes: THE FIRST INSERTION OF AN ADVERTISEMENT THIS CORPUS ALREADY HAS. T-0289 read the same notice in the Democrat of 1834-07-02 with the same copy date of 15 April 1834; this is the printing that copy date belongs to, which is a small but real confirmation that the dateline on a standing advertisement means what it says. The house was already in the town two weeks before Cable took it: the political meeting called in the 1834-04-01 issue was to be held `at the Eagle Hotel at Chicago` on the 16th (that issue's c014), the day AFTER this copy is dated. `has taken` is a succession and Cable is not stated to be the first keeper. The ad gives no address, in April as in July, so the placement is `none` and not a guess.

claims.notes: THE MOST PLACEABLE COURT RECORD IN THE MONTH, and there are two buildings in it. The first is fixed by the plat: a dwelling house on LOT No. 3 IN BLOCK No. 18 in the town of Chicago, in the possession of a Jonathan whose surname is cut. The second is fixed against another building: a SHED OR STORE ROOM adjoining and IN THE REAR OF a store house belonging to J. B. B.` is read from the initial that survives and from the Beaubiens named in this same issue's card of thanks (c009); the levy's `B. Beaubien` alone would not distinguish Jean Baptiste from Mark, and the bracket says so. The block No. 17 fragment belongs to a different item of the same levy and its noun is cut away. Henry Howard's surname is cut to `H¢` and he is not minted.

claims.notes: A LAND HOLDING WRITTEN OUT BY LOT AND BLOCK, and the reason it is a `notice` and not a `building` is that not one of these parcels is said to have anything standing on it. What it IS good for is the plat: the numbers are all in section 16, township 39 north, range 14 east — the school section, the part of the town the state sold in 1833 — and they confirm the block numbering this project already uses. TWO OF THE NUMBERS ARE NOT IN SECTION 16: `water lot No. 11 in Kinzie's addition` is north of the river, and the `visionary interest` in lots 5, 6 and 7 of block 22 is exactly what the lawyer called it — a claim, not a title. Several block numbers are cut and are left as gaps rather than reconstructed by sequence: a wrong block number is a wrong place. `Allen O. T. Breed` is the same man the previous suit attaches; the two spellings differ only in the expansion of the first initial and no merge is declared here.

claims.notes: THE MAIL AS INFRASTRUCTURE, complained about by the man who depended on it. The eastern mail failed to leave Chicago for a week in April 1834 and came back with its own contents — a specific, dated failure of the one link the town had to the Atlantic, in the season the editor says the spring business needed it. It sits beside the post office's other appearance this month, the letter list of 1 April, and the two together are the whole of what April says about the office: it was there, it advertised its uncalled-for letters, and its eastern mail did not always go. It is a Putnam County post office's list of uncalled-for letters, run in the Democrat as out-of-county lists regularly were, and it names people who are not in this town: minting them as Chicago resident candidates is precisely the error ruling 1 does not license. T-0290 made the same call for the Hennepin list of 1 July 1834 and T-0292 for the Hennepin and Plainfield lists of October, so the treatment here is theirs. It is printed at least three times in April — here, at 1834-04-23 (line 3128) and at 1834-04-30 (line 3303) — and the postmaster signs `GALAHER, Jr. P. M.` in a reading the OCR gives four different ways. Zero names minted, six read.

claims.notes: THE 1 APRIL 1834 CHICAGO LETTER LIST, IN A THIRD PRINTING NOBODY KNEW WAS HERE, AND THIS FILE'S OWN EXTRACTION WALKED PAST IT. The list ran on 1834-04-01 (page 3 columns 3 and 4, where 163 names were minted), again on 1834-04-08 (page 3 columns 3 and 4, from which 16 more were minted — the ones the first printing's transcription crushed), and a THIRD time here, on 1834-04-16 page 4 columns 2 and 3, over the same J. S. C. Hogan signature and the same `[on the fir]st day of April, 1834` date line. The month's coverage note and T-0321 both say the list is printed TWICE; it is printed three times. THE REASON THIS ISSUE'S OWN READING MISSED IT is written in this file's note: all eight of page 4's segmenter columns carry the Tesseract fallback banner, so the pass read the town out of page 2 column 8 and page 3 columns 1 and 2 and never opened page 4. THE REASON EVERY KEYWORD SWEEP MISSED IT is the same one that hid 1834-04-01: the heading is cut across two segmenter columns and survives as `List el` / `EMAINIG in 1` in one and `ef Letters FFIC` in the other, so no search for 'list of letters' or 'remaining in the post office' can match. What the sweeps DID find at 1834-04-16 is the HENNEPIN list, on page 3 column 4 — a different list on a different page, and both stand. THE NAMES ARE NOT MINTED AGAIN. T-0292 settled the rule for a list printed more than once — mint it ONCE, from one witness, record the other printings as reprints — and T-0299 is the standing complaint about what happens when it is broken. So the reading is made in full in `normalized`, where it is checkable and citable, and `entities` carries ONLY the two names the first two printings lost outright — Robert Cook and Lewis Doud. That is exactly the rule 1834-04-08's own claims were minted under. TWO FORENAMES THIS PRINTING SUPPLIES ARE READ AND NOT MINTED, AND THE REASON IS A POLICY THE OWNER HAS NOT RULED ON. 1834-04-08 minted `[uncertain: — Duncklo]` and `[uncertain: — Denny]`, surnames with no forename; this printing sets `Hexekial’ Dunchi` and `William Denoy` at the same two positions of the same return. Minting them would put two more people in the gazetteer who are the same two people already in it — the exact harm T-0299 records — and joining them by a declared merge is refused by the compiler, correctly and by design: an unread forename against a read one at the same entry of the same list is T-0392's question and it is BLOCKED ON THE OWNER. So the readings stand in `normalized`, where they are checkable and citable, the two entries stay as 1834-04-08 minted them, and this pass adds two more cases to the pile T-0392 is waiting on. WHAT THIS PRINTING REPAIRS IN THIS HALF, line by line against T-0321's list of eleven debris lines at 1834-04-01 page 3 column 3: line 2914 is HEZEKIAH DUNCKLO — 1834-04-08 read the surname alone (`yy Duncklo`) and minted `[uncertain: — Duncklo]`, and this printing sets `Hexekial’ Dunchi`, which is the forename; line 2915 is LEWIS DOUD, and no other printing holds it at all (1834-04-08 has `ud Bar` at that position); line 2916 is WILLIAM DENNY — 1834-04-08 read `rt Denny` and minted `[uncertain: — Denny]`, and 1834-04-01's own debris reads `inn Renny`, so the surname is settled twice over and the forename comes from here; lines 2922, 2923 and 2925 are Thos. Fitzgerald, H. B. Fowler and James S. Gansodus, already minted from 1834-04-08 and CORROBORATED here by a third witness; lines 2881 and 2882 are the four-name block Harriet Bradford / Eli Benn / Stephen R. Briggs / Robert Cook, of which the first three are minted from 1834-04-08 and the FOURTH IS NOT — Robert Cook stands between Stephen R. Briggs and Enoch Chambers in both this printing and 1834-04-08, it is a separate printed entry from the `Robert G. Cook 2` that stands twelve lines below it in all three printings, and it is minted here. WHAT IT DOES NOT REPAIR: line 2869 (`is Bet i`) has no counterpart in either other printing, which both run Thos. W. Bradley straight into Lewis Benton, so whether a name stood there is not known and nothing is supplied; line 2921 (`Jeter Porter ae`) is debris here too (`Jeter oats`) and in 1834-04-08 (`tl. Jaiee pried Pet`), so it is unread in all three printings; lines 2893 and 2892 are Alonzo Castle and Joseph Chandler, already minted. A LINE NO PRINTING READS AND NO TICKET HAD NAMED: at 1834-04-01 line 2901 (`? Cook`) and here at line 3835 (`p, Cock`) a name stands between James S. Cook and Leander Collins in both printings and is legible in neither. It is recorded, not guessed.

claims.notes: THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME THIRD PRINTING, AND THE BEST WITNESS TO THE J-W HALF OF THE 1 APRIL 1834 LIST THAT THE CORPUS HOLDS. It sets one name per line with no interleaved editorial and no debris line at all, which neither 1834-04-01 nor 1834-04-08 manages. WHAT IT REPAIRS, against T-0321's account of 1834-04-01 page 3 column 4: the SEVEN LINES 3039-3045, where the interleaved editorial took the column, hold FIVE names — Isaac Merrill, Chas. Manning, James Mulford, Philo C. Mills, James McKee — exactly the five 1834-04-08 supplied and already minted, in exactly that order, between Leonard Morse and Henry S. Misner. T-0321 says of those lines that 'what else may have been in those lines is not known'; on this witness nothing else was, and the five are the whole of it. WHAT IT ADDS, and this is where the 179-name floor actually moves: EIGHT names stand in this printing that neither earlier one minted, and all eight are minted here. Samuel Louis and Gregory E. Legg stand between Jacob L. Lansing and Robert Loveland — 1834-04-01 has one garbled line there (`iregory. 1`, which is the forename of the second) and 1834-04-08 has two (`‘amue! i`, `sey erate ‘A ee`), so both are corroborated twice and legible only here. P. F. W. Peck and William Power stand between Robt. Ogilvey and Dudly Peck, where 1834-04-01 has no line at all; 1834-04-08 carries `W, Peek` for the first of them and then loses the column to an editorial. Mason B. Smith stands between Robt. Stephens and Mr. Smith, where 1834-04-01 has the unread `[uncertain: Mason is Sath? PEE:]` and 1834-04-08 has `fnson B. Smith`. Robt. Strong stands between Douglass Sloan and Samuel Shaw, where 1834-04-01 has `[uncertain: Robt. Strong Detroit, ?]` — read there as an advertisement's dateline and not minted — and 1834-04-08 has `pb Strong`. Dr. Trimball, D. V. S. Torry and Elam Tuller stand between George Tryon and Jason B. Vaughan, where 1834-04-01 has one debris line and one unminted fragment (`.V. 8. Torr:`) and 1834-04-08 has `lam Teller`. AND ONE CORRECTION, WHICH IS NOT A NEW NAME BUT A CONFLATION UNDONE: this printing sets `Geo. % Walker` at line 4041 and `G. H. Walker` at line 4046, five lines apart, and 1834-04-08 sets `eo. E. Walker` and `i Walker` at the same two positions. THERE ARE TWO WALKERS IN THIS LIST. 1834-04-01 c002 minted one, normalizing its line 3110 `G. He Walker` as `G[eo]. [E]. Walker` — which is the SECOND Walker wearing the FIRST one's initials, while 1834-04-01 line 3105 (`« . Walker`), the first Walker, was dropped. On three witnesses the first is Geo. E. Walker, standing between Mansfield Wheeler and Jeddiah Woolley, and the second is G. H. Walker, standing between Elihu Walter and Tho. C. Webb. Geo. E. Walker is minted here; 1834-04-01 c002's entity is corrected to G. H. Walker in the same pass, which is where its printed line actually stands. READINGS THIS PRINTING SETTLES WITHOUT MOVING A NAME: at the S run 1834-04-01 reads `Benjamin Reed, the,`, `Ira Raymore apy’` and `3. Geo. Square t 3 first rate` in three consecutive lines of an otherwise unbroken alphabetical block of S surnames. This printing sets `Benjarnin Smith`, `Ira Saymoro` and `Geo. Saver`, and 1834-04-08's own reading of that block is cut too far left to arbitrate. The alphabetical position is with this printing and against 1834-04-01's, but a minted name is not rewritten on a second transcription of equal rank — that is what the page images are for — so the three stand as minted and the disagreement is recorded here. T-0321.
